title: Contracts for work civil servants could do: the Civil Service Commission’s list of 16 June 2025
question: What work did departments ask to contract out instead of hiring City employees, for how much, and how often had they done so before?
finding: The Commission’s list for 16 June 2025 holds 11 requests worth $95.8 million (cumulative $98.2 million); Public Health asked for 4 of them, $80.2 million. 8 say the department had contracted out the same or similar services in the last three years, and in 4 the department answered that the City has employees or classes with the skills. The largest, $30.0 million over 60 months for unarmed guards at the public hospitals and clinics, is marked a temporary basis; the department wrote that the Sheriff’s Office used to do the work: “The San Francisco Sheriff's Office has provided these services but acknowledged that they are experiencing significant staffing challenges, and are unable to provide uninterrupted …”.
how: The amounts, durations and descriptions are read from the item’s summary table; the answers to the form’s questions are read from an OCR of the scanned form pages (the PDF’s text layer for those pages is unreadable). Quotations are cut at 25 words.
limits: Contracting out is permitted when the Commission approves it; State grants can require that money go to community organizations, and some work needs equipment or licenses the City lacks. The OCR can misread a word; the page images are in the item. The item covers one meeting only, so a pattern over years needs the other meetings’ lists.

rows.desc: The Elder Abuse Prevention Program, emanating from the Older Americans Act Title VII, seeks to enable older individuals and adults with disabilities to maintain their well-being through locally developed community-based systems of services to strengthen and implement programs for the prevention, detection, assessment, and treatment of elder abuse. The Department of Disability and Aging Services seeks to effectuate the coordination of interventions and prevention with adult protective services, law enforcement, courts, and other entities. The relevant service areas focus on training in abuse identification and mandated reporting to all agencies as defined by State law, and the establishment and coordination of Multi-Disciplinary Team (MDT) meetings on a regular basis for the benefit of Adult Protective Services (APS) clients through the facilitation of meetings, and in compliance with California law and state mandates. These meetings will gather the appropriate professionals for the review of active APS cases to support the resolution of challenging situations facing our clients (and closed cases in the instance of Elder and Disabled Death Review Team meetings).
